findings.title: Parse the query instead of using a substring to identify error-only searches
findings.body: The presence of `event.type:error` does not mean a Discover query selects only errors. For example, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` both pass this check. For allowlisted projects, their count is then replaced with an aggregation over `sample_weight`, even though the helper explicitly states that transactions do not have that field. These valid searches can consequently fail or return incorrect counts. Determine whether the parsed query actually restricts results to errors before applying the transformation.

findings.title: Check upsampling against the dataset actually being queried
findings.body: The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset`, while query execution uses `scoped_dataset`. These differ in the dashboard splitting paths: a metrics-enhanced request can execute an error-only query against Discover, but this check still sees the metrics dataset and rejects upsampling. As a result, sampled error charts produced by those paths continue to report stored counts rather than estimated counts. Pass the actual scoped dataset and effective query into the eligibility check.

findings.title: Apply weighted counting to top-event selection as well as its time series
findings.body: For top-events requests, only `timeseries_columns` is transformed to weighted counting; `selected_columns` and `orderby` are still passed directly from the original request. A request selecting and ordering by `count()` therefore chooses its top groups using stored-event counts, then plots weighted counts for those groups. With differing client sample rates, a group with fewer stored events can have the largest estimated count and still be excluded from the chart. Transform the selection and ranking aggregates consistently with the time-series aggregate.
